subject: bauhausBird
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: songbird on a branch.
Style: Bauhaus primary-colour geometry.

spec.name: Bauhaus Songbird
spec.description: A small perching songbird assembled from primitive geometry in Bauhaus primary colours (red sphere body, blue head, yellow triangle beak and wings), sitting on a black geometric branch with a block trunk.
spec.layout: Real songbird scale: about 0.30 m from beak tip (z +0.118) to tail tip (z -0.18), head top at y 0.425. The branch is a horizontal black limb along X (x -0.30..0.30, axis y 0.20, radius 0.02, top y 0.22, z 0) with a square trunk post at x -0.24 standing on a flat base plate on y = 0. The bird perches centred at x 0, faces +Z, perpendicular to the branch. From front to back: small yellow beak, a round blue head sphere, a red egg-shaped body, a cream round belly disc on the chest, yellow triangular wings folded along the flanks, and a long flat blue tail slanting down and back with red and yellow bars. Two thin black legs (tarsus) drop from the body and the toes grip the branch top (3 front toes, 1 back toe, each resting at y about 0.224-0.23). Bauhaus language: every form is a pure primitive (sphere, 3-4 sided cone, box, disc, triangle extrude) with hard flat colour. Primary red, yellow, blue plus black and cream. Facets stay visible (low segment counts, 6-10 around). The composition repeats circle / triangle / square: circle = body, head, eyes, cheek discs; triangle = beak, wings, tail tip, branch leaves; square = trunk, base, tail bars. Details (eye rings, wing bars, belly disc, feather stripes) are small separate parts in their own colours seated on the surfaces.

parts.builds: The branch and its stand, all on joint root. A flat square base plate (cream, about 0.12 x 0.012 x 0.12 at x -0.24) on the floor; a square trunk post (black, 0.04 x 0.04, y 0.012..0.2) at x -0.24; the main horizontal branch as an 8-sided black rod/sweep from x -0.30 to x 0.30 along y 0.20, z 0, radius 0.02 (top at y 0.22, so the bird's feet rest on it), with a slight taper to 0.015 at the +x end. Bauhaus decoration: three cream ring bands (thin discs/rods) around the branch at x -0.15, 0.15, 0.24 (not under the bird, clear of |x| < 0.06); a red flat disc and a yellow triangle extrude as leaf motifs on short charcoal twig rods at the +x end and near the trunk, rising no higher than y 0.30 and staying at |x| > 0.12; a blue small cube knot on the trunk; a yellow cap triangle or disc on the branch's cut end at x 0.30 and a red disc on the -x end. No bird anatomy. Nothing at |x| < 0.06 above y 0.225.
parts.attaches: Branch top at perchTop (y 0.22) carries the feet at footL/footR. Stand on floorOrigin.

parts.builds: Body and tail. Red egg-shaped body: sphere scaled to radii x 0.045, y 0.048, z 0.065 at bodyCenter (about 10 x 7 segments, faceted), on joint body. Cream round belly disc/half-sphere seated on the front-lower chest around bellyFront (radius ~0.032, flattened), plus a thin yellow ring disc around it. Blue back saddle: a flattened blue cap over the upper back (a squashed sphere or lathe cap hugging the body top, y up to 0.353), with 3 small yellow triangle chevrons or discs on it as Bauhaus pattern. A small redDeep rump wedge near tailRoot. Tail: a long flat blue tail built as a few overlapping flat boxes/extruded rectangles fanned slightly (centre feather plus two side feathers, thickness 0.004, width about 0.03 total, length from tailRoot to tailTip z -0.18, slanting down to y 0.25) riding tail1/tail2; red and yellow square bar stripes across it (thin boxes in their own colour, seated on top), a yellow triangle tip. Navy undertail coverts block below tail root. The body stays clear of the head sphere (neck mount at neckBase) and leaves room for wings on the flanks (x +-0.043..0.06) and legs at hipL/hipR.
parts.attaches: Neck at neckBase, wings at shoulderL/shoulderR, legs at hipL/hipR, tail begins at tailRoot (joint tail1). Everything else rides body / tail1 / tail2.

parts.builds: Neck, head and beak, the face settled first. Blue head sphere radius 0.036 centred at headCenter (about 10 x 8 segments) on joint head, with a short blue neck collar cylinder/sphere linking neckBase to the head on joint neck. Eyes: on each side at about x +-0.027, y 0.395, z 0.07, a white disc (radius 0.0095), black ring behind, a black pupil disc (0.0055) in front and a tiny white highlight; discs face outward-forward and sit proud of the head sphere surface by about 1 mm. Red round cheek disc (radius 0.012) below and behind each eye. Yellow triangle brow wedge or crown: a small yellow extruded triangle on top of the head (crest) plus a thin black stripe across the crown. Beak: upper beak a yellow 4-sided cone (radius 0.014 base at beakBase, tip at beakTip, slightly flattened vertically) on joint head; lower beak a smaller, shorter yellowPale 4-sided cone below it on joint jaw (hinge jawHinge), a thin gap/black mouth line (thin dark box) between them. Two tiny black nostril dots on the upper beak. Nothing in front of the face. Cream chin/throat disc under the beak on the head.
parts.attaches: Neck base meets the torso at neckBase; head sphere centre headCenter; jaw hinges at jawHinge; beak starts at beakBase and ends at beakTip.

parts.builds: Left and right wings (mirror with +x = left), folded against the flanks but slightly separate from the body. Each wing: a yellow main triangular extruded slab (thickness about 0.008, shoulder at shoulderL/R, broad at the front, pointing back to a tip near z -0.13, y about 0.27, x about +-0.058) on joint wingL/wingR, following the flank so its inner face sits at x about +-0.044..0.05 (just outside the body's side at those heights). Layered Bauhaus feather shapes on the outside face: a smaller blue triangle covert layer near the shoulder, a red disc/half-disc spot, 3 long thin primary strips (navy, blue, red) stacked towards the tip riding wingL2/wingR2 with slightly fanned angles, a thin black outline strip along the leading edge, and a white small square bar. Each wing is a clear assembly of 8-14 pieces. Wings stay inside x +-0.07 and do not touch the tail attachments or head.
parts.attaches: Roots at shoulderL / shoulderR on the body flanks; tips trail towards tailRoot's side, beside the tail.

parts.builds: Both legs and feet. Each leg: a short feathered cream thigh tuft (small sphere/cone) at hipL/hipR just hiding the body underside, a thin black tarsus rod (radius 0.0035, 6 sides) from the hip down to the ankle at y 0.228 (x +-0.022), a small yellow ankle ball. Four toes per foot from the ankle: two front toes angled slightly apart forward (+z up to z +0.035) and one longer back toe (hallux) to z -0.022, each a thin black rod radius 0.003-0.004 with a small yellow claw tip (tiny cone) and a small black knuckle sphere; toes rest on the branch top, lying at y about 0.224-0.23 and curling down slightly at the ends, with bottoms touching but not deeper than y 0.221 (branch top 0.22). Left and right legs mirror in x.
parts.attaches: Hips at hipL/hipR under the body; feet at footL/footR on the perchTop.

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching out a spec for a songbird perched on a branch in a Bauhaus primary-colour geometric style. The bird is roughly 0.16 to 0.18 m including its tail, and the branch around 0.4 to 0.5 m, so I'm working out how the branch should run along the x axis relative to the bird's facing direction.

I'm working out whether the branch should run along the X axis, with the bird facing +Z, and settling on a rough footprint of about 0.5 m wide and 0.3 m deep. Since the branch shouldn't float, I'm considering a small trunk block resting on the floor that rises into a horizontal limb near y≈0.2, while also weighing whether a separate stand is needed. I'm also planning to split the bird into rigged parts (body and tail, head, wings, legs and feet) so the joints and coordinates line up across them.

I'm settling the branch geometry: a radius around 0.02 m, its top at y≈0.22, running along x and centred on z=0, so the feet can rest on it. I'm also picking a Bauhaus palette of red, yellow, blue, black and cream, and starting to assign those colours to the bird's body, belly, head, beak and wings.

I'm settling on the colour scheme now: a blue head with a yellow beak and white-and-black eyes, a red body with a cream belly patch, and yellow wings edged in blue.

I'm working out the bird's proportions now, with the body centred just above the branch and the head sitting higher and forward. I'm also weighing how the tail trails behind it, with blue slabs and a yellow tip, and how the branch base might be built as a simple geometric block.

I'm finishing the tail and wing placement, with the wings folded against the body and a small gap between them. I'm also settling the overall size, a width of about 0.6 m, and adding a short twig on the branch's far end.

I'm laying out the rest of the spec: the trunk base as a plate on the floor with a post rising into the branch, and the tail's z-extent and overall size of about 0.6 by 0.43 by 0.30 m. I'm also considering a second small twig on the +x side, and I'm defining the joint hierarchy starting from a root body joint.

I'm defining the joint chain for the bird's rig: the body as the spine root, then a neck, head, and a jaw joint for the beak, with the tail built from a couple of joints running back from the body.

I'm placing the leg and foot joints for the rig: hips tucked into the body, ankles just above the branch, and the toes resting on its top surface.

I'm placing the ankle joints at about y=0.228 with the toe joints set just above the branch top, so the toes can rest on it.

I'm listing the anchor points for the spec: the branch top, the foot and hip positions, and the shoulder and neck base. The branch top stays at y=0.22 with the toes resting just above it.

I'm checking the head, beak and tail positions against the body, and working out the overall box: the length runs about 0.30 m along z, and the height comes to roughly 0.43 m.

I'm working out the perch as a floor-anchored part with a trunk base, branch, twigs and Bauhaus leaf motifs, with the twig leaves rising above the bird's height at the ends away from it. I'm still weighing which joint, if any, the perch should attach to, since it shouldn't move with the bird.

I'm settling the root joint as a plain "root" at the origin, with no role, so the perch rides on it and the body hangs from it. The next part is the torso, covering the body, belly, back, rump and the tail joints.

I'm now specifying the torso parts, covering the body, belly, back, rump and tail, with a box running from about z -0.18 to 0.06. For the head, I'm listing the neck, crown, eyes, cheeks and upper and lower beak, with the jaw joint at the front. The wings get their own box with primaries and covert layers, and the legs and feet are laid out with the toes extending forward and back over the branch.

I'm finalizing the part budgets: perch 180, torso 200, head 180, wings 160, and legs 100, for a total of 820, which is under the 900 limit. Next I'm assigning the head's neck and head joints, plus a jaw joint at the front of the head, and I'm working out the wing joints and how far they sit from the body.

I'm choosing a flat palette of red, yellow, blue, black, cream and a few shades, and I'm deciding the branch will be black with cream rings while the base plate might be grey.

I'm settling the palette as bark black #1a1a1d and charcoal #2e2e33, and now I'm going to write out the JSON.
